title: Sun Altitude Calculator: How High Is the Sun?
description: Find the Sun's altitude above the horizon for any place and time with the Sun Altitude Calculator — noon peaks, seasons and shadows. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, the Sun's noon altitude over New York swings from 72.7° on June 21 to just 25.9° on December 21 — the single number that explains winter's weakness.
quick_answer: The Sun Altitude Calculator reports how high the Sun stands above your horizon — its altitude in degrees — for any place, date and time. Enter the details and read the angle: the number behind shadow lengths, solar gain, glare and whether the Sun clears the building across the street.
steps_intro: Altitude is the Sun's height, measured like an angle on a protractor:

body.t: spends: give it your hour's altitude and fences become numbers.
South glass in summer versus winter is an altitude story — high June sun shades easily, low December sun pours in. Design with both numbers.
The blinding commute happens when the Sun's altitude sits in the windscreen band at your driving hour — check the dates it starts and ends.
Higher Sun, stronger UV (roughly): a noon altitude under ~25° is why northern winters make almost no vitamin D.
Noon altitude, computed: New York 72.7° (June) versus 25.9° (December); London 61.9° versus 15.1°. London's December Sun never climbs higher than a fist-and-a-half above the horizon.
At the equator the noon altitude touches 90° — Sun directly overhead — around the equinoxes (89.5° computed for March 20). Shadowless noon is a real place and time.

popular_table.intro: Solar-noon altitude at the solstices — the year's ceiling and floor.
popular_table.note: Noon altitude = 90° − |latitude − solar declination|. The equator's solstice dips are the tropics' signature: the noon Sun leans north in June, south in December.

faq: The Sun's angular height above the horizon: 0° at the horizon, 90° directly overhead, negative below the horizon (night).
From solar declination and the hour angle for your place and time — the standard astronomical formula, the same engine as the Solar Position Calculator.
Why is winter's noon Sun so low?
Your hemisphere leans away: the noon altitude falls by twice the axial tilt (about 47°) between solstices at mid-latitudes.
Can the Sun be overhead here?
Only between the tropics, where latitude can equal the Sun's declination — never in the US mainland or Europe.
Zenith = 90° − altitude; solar engineers quote zenith, everyone else altitude. Same fact, two doors.
Within a small fraction of a degree for the Sun's centre — the Sun's own face spans half a degree, which sets the meaningful precision.
Geometric altitude is reported; near the horizon the air lifts the apparent Sun by ~0.5°, which the sunrise tools fold in.
